 News Porsche Latest Porsche 911 & 718 recall reaches Australia; 77 models affected
 By 
 Rohan S. 
 October 27, 2026 
 1 Min Read 
 SHARE 
 Porsche has issued a recall in Australia covering 77 examples of its 911 and 718 sports cars built in 2024, following a defect that could cause a wheel to detach while driving. The issue involves the centre-lock wheel nuts, which may fracture due to a manufacturing defect.
 The recall covers several high-performance models from the 992-generation 911 range, including the Carrera GTS, GT3, GT3 RS, S/T, Turbo and Turbo S. Two particularly focused driver’s cars, the 718 Cayman GT4 RS and 718 Spyder RS, are also affected.
 According to the official recall notice, a fractured centre-lock nut could allow a wheel to loosen and come off the car. That could lead to a sudden loss of stability and control, potentially causing a serious accident involving occupants, other road users or bystanders.
 Porsche will contact affected owners and ask them to book an appointment at an authorised service centre. The necessary work will be carried out free of charge.
 Earlier this month, Porsche also issued this recall in the US , covering 548 vehicles, with owners of the affected cars receiving a “Do Not Drive” warning.
